free_tier.stated: "Small projects may request up to 8'000 node hours on Alps. Such projects may not exceed the granted allocation and are limited to a one-year duration." A Preparatory Project is the entry step and "is allocated a total of 250 node hours over 3 months on the HPC vCluster on Alps". Small proposals are assessed by technical evaluation only, with acceptance "within two months from submission", and no fixed deadline.

chaining: The quarterly reset is what makes this record useful beyond a simple rejection: a 8,000 node-hour annual allocation arrives in three-month windows and expires unused, so a workload that needs a continuous month of GPU time does not fit the shape even inside the institution.

notes: The smallest CSCS door, the Preparatory Project at 250 node hours, is also the one most often described as open, and the same postdoctoral-position requirement applies to it. A node on Alps is a GH200 Grace Hopper node, so a node hour is one GH200 hour rather than one core hour, which matters when comparing the 8,000 figure with the core-hour numbers elsewhere in this record.
